title: When will the RSA-2048 challenge number be factorized by a quantum computer?
description:
[RSA-2048](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSA_numbers#RSA-2048) is a seminal challenge in cryptography and computing, representing a 617-digit number that is the product of two prime numbers. It was published by RSA Laboratories as part of their [RSA Factoring Challenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSA_Factoring_Challenge) to encourage research in computational number theory and the practical difficulty of factoring large numbers.

The challenge has significant implications for cybersecurity, as the [RSA encryption system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSA_\(cryptosystem\))'s security relies on the computational difficulty of factoring such large numbers. While classical computers would require impractical amounts of time to factor RSA-2048, quantum computers using Shor's algorithm [could theoretically accomplish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-quantum_cryptography) this task in a feasible timeframe.

Current quantum computers face several key challenges:

1. Achieving sufficient quantum bits (qubits) while maintaining coherence
2. Implementing error correction at scale
3. Developing the precise quantum circuits needed for Shor's algorithm

Experts estimate that factoring RSA-2048 [would require](https://research.kudelskisecurity.com/2021/08/24/quantum-attack-resource-estimate-using-shors-algorithm-to-break-rsa-vs-dh-dsa-vs-ecc/) a minimum of 4098 of stable, error-corrected qubits, while current quantum computers typically have fewer than 1,000 noisy qubits. The achievement of this milestone would represent a fundamental breakthrough in quantum computing capability and would have profound implications for current cryptographic systems.

resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **January 1** of the year in which RSA-2048 is first successfully factorized by a quantum computer, according to credible sources. If this has not happened before January 1, 2075, this question will resolve as **>2074-12-31**.
fine_print: If RSA-2048 is factorized by a non-quantum computer first, this question will be **Annulled**.
